title: Delaware Statutory Trust Act
summary: Delaware Statutory Trust Act governs the creation, administration, and operation of statutory trusts formed under Delaware law. Distinguishes between statutory trusts and common-law express trusts. Governs trust business operations, trustee powers, investor rights, and series structures.
limitations: Source verification is not professional legal approval.
Session law should be checked against current compiled statutes before professional use.
The DSTA does not apply to ordinary private family trusts unless specifically elected.

title: Delaware Trust Act
summary: Delaware Trust Act governs common-law express trusts formed under Delaware law. Covers trust creation, validity, interpretation, modification, termination, trustee duties, beneficiary rights, and creditor claims against trusts.
limitations: Source verification is not professional legal approval.
Does not resolve fact-specific capacity, undue influence, or trust interpretation disputes.
Statutory trust rules under the DSTA are distinct and not incorporated here.

title: Delaware Qualified Dispositions in Trust Act (DAPT)
summary: Delaware Qualified Dispositions in Trust Act (DAPT) provides asset protection for self-settled trusts. Allows a settlor to transfer assets to an irrevocable trust and obtain protection from the settlor's own creditors, subject to specific statutory requirements, transferor-benefit provisions, and time limitations.
limitations: Source verification is not professional legal approval.
Bankruptcy courts may apply federal bankruptcy law to disregard state DAPT provisions.
Federal tax claims, family support obligations, and certain government claims remain exceptions.
Transferor's own creditor claims may survive if the transfer was fraudulent.
Self-settled DAPT requires genuine relinquishment of control and other strict conditions.

title: Delaware Directed Trust Act
summary: Delaware Directed Trust Act governs trusts with directed trustee structures. Authorizes appointment of a directed trustee, investment direction holder, and administrative agent. Defines fiduciary duties of directed trustees and exculpation provisions for following directed instructions.
limitations: Source verification is not professional legal approval.
Directed trustee remains liable for following an improper direction.
Federal fiduciary duty laws may override exculpation provisions in certain ERISA contexts.

title: Trust Protector
summary: Delaware Trust Act provisions for trust protectors. Defines trust protector powers, including power to direct trust modifications, remove and appoint trustees, amend trust terms, and consent to trustee actions. Trust protectors owe fiduciary duties unless exculpated by the trust instrument.
limitations: Source verification is not professional legal approval.
Exculpatory language in trust instrument controls scope of trust protector duties.
Court may review protector actions for abuse of discretion.

title: Trustee Fiduciary Duties
summary: Delaware Trust Act fiduciary duty provisions for trustees. Covers duty of loyalty, prudent investor rule, impartiality, administration costs, information to beneficiaries, and delegation. Includes exculpation and indemnification provisions.
limitations: Source verification is not professional legal approval.
Exculpatory clauses in trust instruments may limit but not eliminate willful misconduct liability.
Prudent investor rule applies to entire trust portfolio, not individual investments.

title: Delaware UCC Article 9
summary: Delaware's adoption of Revised UCC Article 9. Governs secured transactions, financing statements, perfection, priority, and collateral enforcement. Establishes the Delaware filing office for UCC liens, including central, local, fixture, and transmitting utility filings.
limitations: Source verification is not professional legal approval.
Filing office acceptance does not establish attachment, enforceability, ownership, priority, or collateral validity.
Federal bankruptcy law may override state perfection and priority rules.

title: Delaware Homestead and Exempt Property
summary: Delaware homestead and exempt property provisions. Provides exemptions for a debtor's primary residence, certain personal property, and wages from garnishment or levy.
limitations: Source verification is not professional legal approval.
Federal bankruptcy exemptions and ERISA-qualified retirement accounts may provide additional protection.
Exemptions are subject to claim amounts and eligibility conditions.

title: Trust Decanting
summary: Delaware trust decanting statute. Authorizes a trustee with discretionary power to make distributions to distribute trust assets to a second trust (trust A into trust B) for the benefit of beneficiaries, extending trust duration, modifying terms, or improving asset protection.
limitations: Source verification is not professional legal approval.
Decanting does not eliminate existing beneficiary rights without consent.
A power of appointment exercised in the decanting instrument has separate legal requirements.
Bankruptcy trustee may challenge a decanting that defrauded creditors.

title: Nonjudicial Settlement Agreements and Trust Modification
summary: Delaware nonjudicial settlement agreements and trust modification. Authorizes interested parties to modify, terminate, or reform a trust without judicial proceedings through a valid nonjudicial settlement agreement, subject to court approval for certain matters.
limitations: Source verification is not professional legal approval.
Court approval required if the agreement does not fairly resolve the interests of all parties.
Charitable trust modifications require Attorney General involvement.

title: Governing Law and Principal Place of Administration
summary: Delaware governing law and principal place of administration. Establishes that Delaware law governs the validity, construction, and administration of a trust if the trust instrument designates Delaware law or if the trust instrument is silent and the trustee is a Delaware trustee.
limitations: Source verification is not professional legal approval.
Other states may apply their own conflict-of-laws rules to determine governing law.
Federal courts may apply a different choice-of-law analysis in certain contexts.

title: Revocable Trusts and Settlor Powers
summary: Delaware revocable trust provisions. Governs the creation, amendment, and revocation of revocable trusts. Settlor retains power to revoke, modify, or terminate a revocable trust during lifetime. Settlor's creditors may reach revocable trust assets.
limitations: Source verification is not professional legal approval.
Revocable trust assets remain exposed to settlor's creditors during lifetime.
Death does not insulate a revocable trust from estate settlement obligations.

title: Spendthrift Trusts
summary: Delaware spendthrift trust provisions. Validates spendthrift clauses that restrain a beneficiary's ability to assign or anticipate trust distributions. Enforces creditor limitations on trust distributions, subject to statutory exceptions for support, taxes, and certain government claims.
limitations: Source verification is not professional legal approval.
Settlor's own creditors cannot reach trust distributions if the settlor is not also a beneficiary.
Exception creditors including child support and alimony may reach spendthrift protected distributions.
Self-settled spendthrift protection is limited to DAPT-qualified transfers.

title: Certification of Trust
summary: Delaware trust certification statute. Authorizes a trustee to provide a certification of trust (rather than the full trust instrument) to third parties. Certification must include the trust's existence, the trustee's powers, the信托's amendment procedures, and the信托's revocability status.
limitations: Source verification is not professional legal approval.
A third party who relies on a certification may be protected only if the certification is accurate.
A certification that omits material terms may limit the trustee's ability to enforce agreements.

title: Charitable Trusts and Cy Pres
summary: Delaware charitable trust provisions. Governs the creation, administration, and modification of charitable trusts. Includes cy pres doctrine for modifying charitable purposes when the original purpose becomes impracticable or impossible.
limitations: Source verification is not professional legal approval.
Delaware Attorney General has oversight authority over charitable trusts.
Cy pres modification requires court proceedings and AG involvement.

citation: Delaware Department of Finance, Division of Revenue — Taxpayer Information Publication
title: Delaware Trust Income Tax Guidance
summary: Delaware Division of Revenue guidance on trust income tax. Delaware imposes a trust income tax on certain Delaware situs trusts. Resident trusts and nonresident trusts with Delaware source income may have filing obligations.
limitations: Source verification is not professional legal approval.
Tax advice requires a licensed tax professional.
Delaware estate tax was repealed effective January 1, 2015.
Federal estate tax rules and Delaware filing requirements should be reviewed separately.

title: Successor trustees
summary: Governs the appointment and powers of successor trustees when a vacancy occurs.
